newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares dive at noon, following A shares.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares dive at noon, following A shares.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign B share index tumbled on Thursday morning, following steep falls on the domestic A share market in response to rumours of official plans to further rein in the markets, brokers said.
The B share index plunged 7.18 points or 4.96 percent to 137.54 on turnover of HK$21 million.
B shares did not trade in Shenzhen from Monday to Wednesday to mark the Chinese takeover of Hong Kong.
The A index shed 19.07 points or 4.42 percent to 412.05 on turnover of 3.2 billion yuan after a 4.07 percent fall on Wednesday.
"The market was pushed down by apprehension over possible Beijing plans to further tighten its grip on stock speculation," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
The conclusion of the Hong Kong handover, which has long been a major support for sentiment, also capped buying interest, brokers said.
"More investors pulled out and edged to the sidelines after the handover euphoria falied to produce a miracle in yesterday's A share market," the J&A analyst said.
"The B share technical charts look bad after the morning's decline. More losses are likely," a stock analyst at Hainan Provincial Trust and Investment Co said in Shenzhen.
Many analysts had expected the 140-point level to provide a strong support.
"But a minor rebound in the B share market may occur soon due to the thin turnover," the Hainan analyst said.
In the A share market, market barometer Shenzhen Development Bank dropped 1.13 yuan to 35.00 yuan on heavy volume of 7.2 million shares after hitting a low of 34.55 yuan.
In the B share market, Livzon Pharmaceutical was the weakest performer with a loss of HK$0.50 or 9.71 percent to HK$4.65. (c) Reuters Limited 1997
